newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower across the board in moderate trade following a slight decline in the interbank rate, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly after a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill rates were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.10/99.15 compared with last Thursday's close of S$98.68/98.73, September 2001 at S$98.20/98.25 against S$97.40/97.45 and June 2003 at S$96.20/96.25 from S$95.40/95.45.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 5/8 1/2 percent versus last Thursday's 1 7/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 0.73/0.68 percent against last Thursday's yield of 1.25/1.20 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.35/1.30 percent from 1.75/1.70 percent.
